title: Faculty of Pharmacy hosts Sustainable Pharmacy Summer School for the first time in Finland
content:
The summer school has previously taken place at the University of Freiburg (2022 and 2024), Kiel University (2023), and Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg (2025). Participants included representatives from academia, agencies, the healthcare sector and the pharmaceutical industry. "Four days of insightful presentations and engaging discussions," was how the organisers summed up the event.

The programme combined expert lectures, group discussions, a poster session, and plenty of opportunities for international networking. Each day had its own theme:

  • Monday – Planetary Health. The day set the stage by defining health within the broader context of planetary health, addressing the threat posed by climate change to shared health as well as silent pandemics, along with ethical considerations and equity in access to healthcare and pharmaceuticals.
  • Tuesday – Pharmaceutical Development. The focus was on sustainable practices in pharmaceutical development, including formulations and manufacturing processes, the "sustainable-by-design" approach, and advances in sustainable analytical chemistry.

title: DogRisk in the media – Autumn 2026
content:
The first results from the DogRisk weight-loss study were featured in Yle's evening news and accompanying online article. The coverage touched on the high prevalence of canine obesity in Finland and presented findings showing that overweight dogs reached a healthy weight faster than expected on both raw food and dry food diets, but resulted in differences in body composition between the two feeding approaches.

Dr. Anna Hielm-Björkman was a guest on The Pet Food Science Podcast Show in a special International Dog Day episode titled "Canine Nutrition Beyond Diet Labels".

The podcast discusses how dietary patterns may relate to canine gut health and chronic disease, drawing on research into raw and dry feeding, microbiota, metabolomics, dietary interventions, and nutrient composition. The conversation also highlights the importance of moving beyond associations to uncover the biological mechanisms that influence canine health.

title: Salla Saastamoinen tuo kolmen vuosikymmenen EU-kokemuksen Helsingin yliopistoon
content:
After earning a Licentiate of Laws degree at the University of Helsinki, Salla Saastamoinen worked at the European Commission for more than three decades, advancing from specialist duties to the senior leadership of the Commission. Her latest position was Deputy Director-General of the European Anti-Fraud Office (OLAF), where she has also served as Acting Director-General. Previously she served in similar positions as Deputy Director-General of the Commission’s Joint Research Centre (JRC) and as Acting Director-General of the Directorate-General for Justice and Consumers. Now she is returning to the University of Helsinki in an entirely new role.

“This feels inspiring and invigorating. I like new beginnings. Even though I’m returning to a familiar place, the University, Helsinki and Finland have surely all changed in the last 30 years that I have spent working in Brussels and the European Commission,” surmises Saastamoinen.

title: Tutkimukseen pohjautuva Hiilimetsä visualisoi hiilen kiertoa suomalaisessa metsässä
content:
is an interactive, browser-based visualisation of the carbon cycle at different stages of a Finnish forest's rotation period. It offers anyone interested in the topic an easy and illustrative way to explore how carbon moves through forests. Carbon Forest shows when forests act as carbon sinks, when they are carbon sources, and which kinds of forests make the best carbon stores.

Developed at the University of Helsinki, Carbon Forest is aimed at anyone who wants a basic understanding of how the carbon cycle works in Finnish forests. It is also suitable for use in science education. The service also provides concise, easy-to-understand descriptions of the most common forest characteristics from the perspectives of both the carbon cycle and biodiversity.

Carbon Forests' data are based on the SMEAR measurement network of the University of Helsinki's Institute for Atmospheric and Earth System Research (INAR), its long-term measurements and the scientific publications based on them. Carbon Forest is part of the online service.

title: Kasvu Therapeutics kehittää uutta tapaa hoitaa masennusta
content:
The drug development company Kasvu Therapeutics (Kasvu) put out announcing it has raised €30 million to develop pharmaceuticals for the treatment of major depressive disorder and other brain diseases. The amount is the largest ever raised for a Finnish pharmaceutical development company at the preclinical stage. 

The financing round was led by Norwegian venture capital investor Hadean Ventures focusing on drug development and health industry innovations. Finnish participants in the financing round included Tesi (Finnish Industry Investment Ltd), Innovestor Life Science Fund, Nordic Science Investments, Finnish Drug Discovery Center Ltd, Stephen Industries and University of Helsinki Funds.

The funding helps Kasvu’s lead drug candidate KTX-0141, meant for the treatment of depression, to proceed to initial clinical trials. It is expected to be trialled in humans as early as summer 2027. 

Kasvu’s story is based on long-term work by research groups of Neuroscience Center Research Director Eero Castrén and Professor of Biophysics Ilpo Vattulainen.

title: Luonnontieteellisen museon Elämän historia -sali sulkeutuu vuodenvaihteen jälkeen – uusi näyttely avautuu loppuvuodesta 2028
content:
The Natural History Museum’s History of Life is one of the museum’s most popular exhibitions. However, the exhibition, completed in 2008, has long been in need of an update, as it is outdated both in terms of content and exhibition technology.

– The new exhibition will present evolution and the development of biodiversity in a more spectacular and tangible way than before. This is the museum’s most significant renewal project in years, says Sanna Vuori, Head of the Public Engagement Unit at the Finnish Museum of Natural History.

The dinosaurs Giganotosaurus carolinii and Shunosaurus lii in the History of Life exhibition have become familiar to many museum visitors over the years. They will remain in the new exhibition but will be joined by never-before-seen reconstructions of prehistoric animals. Among other things, a reconstruction of the otter-like early whale Ambulocetus natans is currently being built in the museum’s conservation facilities.

title: Southnord Artfest 2026: Roots En Route
content:
Roots En Route is a multi-sensory installation by four artists who will create a multi-sensory installation in dialogue with the greenhouses – examining rootedness and displacement; asking what grows where it was planted and what survives the crossing. The African plants that fill the greenhouses carry their own histories of movement and adaptation.

Camille Norment in collaboration with Sofia Jernberg create a soundscape drawing on the insects and birds of the plants' homelands. Toubab Holmes' site-specific scent installation traces the hidden journeys of plants through the extractive system of perfumery. Charmaine Watkiss visits the botanical legacies and healing traditions of her Caribbean ancestry through large-scale drawings of Plant Warriors. Together, the three works read the botanical garden as an archive of movement, and the plants in it as things that were carried, taken and made to travel.

Running from October 2026 through January 2027, the exhibition offers a long, unhurried encounter between art and the plant world. Set aside more time than you think you need. Walk slowly, sense carefully, and let yourself be immersed.

title: “Ilman pölyttäjiä maailma olisi ankea ja väritön” – Uusi näyttely avaa oven pölyttäjien kiehtovaan elämään
content:
Pollinators represent an astonishingly diverse group of animals, many of which possess remarkable abilities despite their small size. Bees can count, bumblebees solve problems, and on distant islands, even lizards can pollinate flowers.

The  exhibition, which combines science and art, offers a wealth of information, stunning visuals, and fun activities for visitors of all ages. Guests can play interactive games like "Identify the Pollinators" and "Pollinator Protection Bingo," design their own imaginary pollinator, and explore the museum's impressive collection of specimens. The exhibition is based on a newly illustrated non-fiction book.

– We want to show the world through the eyes of pollinators, says exhibition scriptwriter Mia Rönkä, Adjunct Professor in Environmental Ecology at the University of Turku. Rönkä has written the exhibition’s informational texts and poems.

Although the sensory perceptions, cognitive abilities, and communication methods of pollinators like bees differ from ours as humans, we can still strive to understand and appreciate them as individuals of other species – without anthropomorphizing them, Rönkä explains.

title: Ukrainan sota - yliopiston suositukset
content:
The University of Helsinki has condemned the military action by Russia and expressed its support for Ukraine and its university community. We have also expressed our support for Ukraine, together with other Finnish universities, through statements by and the . As a demonstration of support, we have illuminated buildings in the colours of the Ukrainian flag and raised the flag on our premises.

One of the principles of the University of Helsinki is to promote international collaboration in research and higher education, and to support these efforts even in difficult circumstances. Russia’s indefensible military aggression in Ukraine has required exceptional measures, which include those taken in the collaboration between universities.

The University of Helsinki is monitoring both national and EU-level sanctions, adapting our policies and processes accordingly. Together with other Finnish and international universities, the University of Helsinki strives to promote the end of military action in Ukraine, while supporting Ukrainian institutions and people.

title: DH välipalat for early career researchers
content:
In 2025 we launched a series of discussions among early-career researchers in social sciences and humanities to facilitate peer-support and network opportunities for doctoral and early career stage researchers working with similar methods or types of data. The community now has its own . These “välipalat” or evening snacks were inspired by Prof. Meredith Martin, head of the  at Princeton and scholar of historical poetics. In a  at the 2024 DARIAH Annual event, she made a compelling account of the emotional practices involved in creating a DH department. Frustration, incomprehension and helplessness were some feelings that described the fact that humanists were worked up about data. These feelings were the first stepping stone towards building humanities infrastructures. 

The process that followed could be summarized as knocking on doors. Collecting experiences and stumbling blocks from peers empowered professor Martin to knock on higher doors delivering their needs in a volume that administration and funding bodies could not deny. That is how she built an infrastructure to start curing “digital helplessness”.
